question: why did both EfficientNet-Lite4 variants miss the stored reference?
answer: they did not. The reference was wrong, not the compiler.
method: each variant was run against two ONNX Runtime references, one from a default session and one from a session with graph optimisation disabled, so that the reference reflects the graph as written
cause: ONNX Runtime's default optimisation level rewrites DequantizeLinear -> Conv -> QuantizeLinear into an integer kernel. That is a different numerical path from the QDQ graph the compiler is asked to implement, and on this model the two differ by 1.68e-3, which was being charged to the compiler as an error. Joggle reproduces the graph as written to 7.5e-9.
fix: gen_reference.py and subject_ort.py both disable graph optimisation, so every system executes the graph as written and the reference is the literal semantics. The fix is general rather than per-model: it moves the float models' references by at most 3.3e-6 against a 1e-4 tolerance, so no existing verdict depends on it.
consequence: EfficientNet-Lite4 QDQ enters the campaign and is the strongest result in it: 1139.371 ms to 350.123 ms, 3.25x, with ONNX Runtime at 43.342 ms on the same reference.
